title: Make upcoming renewals easy to understand
trigger: Customers encounter a renewal charge without remembering the amount, date, or account involved.
action: Prepare a clear notice showing the verified renewal date, amount or calculation basis, billing interval, and direct management route. Deliver it only through the authorized service-communication process and applicable preferences.
mechanism: Predictable renewal can reduce billing surprise and support deliberate continued use.
guardrail: Match the actual contract and provider state; do not treat a reminder as permission to change terms.
measure: Retained paid customers; renewal disputes and unwanted charges.

title: Reflect the customer's realized value
trigger: Subscribers cannot readily recall the useful work they accomplished with the product.
action: Provide a concise account-level value summary drawn from verified outcomes, such as reports used or workflows completed. Let the customer inspect the underlying activity and relate it to their stated goal.
mechanism: Making real progress visible may strengthen the reason for continued use.
guardrail: Avoid invented time or money savings and exclude demo, failed, or duplicate activity.
measure: Retained useful use; misleading-value complaints and disengagement.

title: Repair stalled workflows before requesting engagement
trigger: An inactive customer stopped using the product after a failed job, yet receives generic reminders to return.
action: Detect the unresolved workflow state, make the recovery action clear, and preserve the work needed to resume. If outreach is authorized, reference the specific solvable issue rather than sending a generic promotion.
mechanism: Removing the reason for disengagement can be more relevant than asking for another visit.
guardrail: Do not expose sensitive diagnostics in messages or assume inactivity always means a product failure.
measure: Recovered useful workflows; repeat failures and support burden.

title: Route failed payments to the right owner
trigger: A subscription loses access while payment-recovery messages reach someone who cannot update billing.
action: Identify the authorized billing owner and provide the provider-supported payment-update action with the real status and timing. Coordinate with existing retry rules and suppress recovery prompts after confirmed resolution.
mechanism: A clear actionable route can recover an intended subscription without adding confusion.
guardrail: Do not start competing retry jobs or send unauthorized messages; preserve the agreed access policy.
measure: Recovered collections with continued use; duplicate charges and complaints.

title: Restore expired integrations without rebuilding setup
trigger: A once-useful workflow silently stops after an external permission or credential expires.
action: Show the broken connection, its impact on the customer's work, and a secure reauthorization path that preserves configuration. Confirm when processing resumes and identify any backlog requiring user review.
mechanism: A recoverable connection failure can preserve the customer's accumulated setup investment.
guardrail: Request only required access and avoid replaying consequential actions without appropriate confirmation.
measure: Restored recurring workflows; silent data gaps and repeated churn reasons.

title: Transfer ownership when the champion leaves
trigger: A team depends on one administrator who leaves the company or stops managing the product.
action: Offer authorized account owners a clear transfer process for billing responsibility, integrations, and key workflows. Provide a concise handover view so a successor can understand the existing setup and useful outputs.
mechanism: Continuity can prevent organizational change from erasing the product's established value.
guardrail: Verify authority, remove former access appropriately, and do not transfer personal credentials or private data blindly.
measure: Retained team accounts; orphaned billing and access incidents.

title: Offer a genuine pause for seasonal gaps
trigger: Customers cancel because their need temporarily ends rather than because the product fails.
action: If commercially supported, offer an optional pause with exact charge, access, data, and resumption rules. Keep cancellation equally clear and let the customer choose a period appropriate to their actual gap.
mechanism: A fitting temporary state may preserve continuity without charging for unwanted ongoing service.
guardrail: Do not invent pause support or resume billing under undisclosed conditions; treat new pause terms as a commercial proposal.
measure: Paused accounts returning to paid use; unexpected resumes and refunds.

title: Offer a suitable downgrade before overpayment
trigger: A customer consistently uses far less capacity than their current plan and is considering leaving.
action: Show a supported lower-cost plan that still meets the customer's actual needs, including any features or limits they would lose. Let an authorized buyer review the change effect before confirming.
mechanism: A better fit may preserve a satisfied customer who otherwise sees the whole subscription as wasteful.
guardrail: Do not assume low usage proves low value or silently remove required capabilities.
measure: Retained accounts and contribution; downgrade-related failures.

title: Make a retention alternative optional and relevant
trigger: The cancellation flow shows the same discount or intervention regardless of why the customer wants to leave.
action: Offer at most a relevant supported alternative based on an optional reason, such as a simpler plan or help with an unresolved task. Keep a direct cancellation action available through the decision.
mechanism: A relevant alternative can address a solvable obstacle without turning exit into a struggle.
guardrail: Do not require a survey, repeated refusals, or a call; introduce commercial incentives only with authorization.
measure: Voluntary retained use; cancellation completion and complaints.

title: Keep data export usable at exit
trigger: Customers worry that leaving the product will trap their work, making both initial purchase and later renewal feel risky.
action: Provide the promised export route with clear scope, supported formats, and the actual access deadline. Help the customer verify the export rather than placing it behind a retention offer.
mechanism: Confidence in control over accumulated work may reduce distrust and make future return easier.
guardrail: Honor data-retention and access policies; do not claim exports are complete when important supported content is missing.
measure: Successful exports and later returns; trapped-data complaints.

title: Confirm cancellation and remaining access clearly
trigger: A customer clicks cancel but cannot tell whether future charges have actually stopped.
action: Show the verified cancellation state, effective date, remaining access, and any relevant data deadline. Provide a durable confirmation through the authorized channel and update account controls accordingly.
mechanism: A clear final state can preserve trust even when the current subscription ends.
guardrail: Distinguish period-end cancellation, immediate termination, pause, and refund; reconcile with provider state.
measure: Correct cancellations; unwanted renewal charges and repeat contacts.

title: Explain the next renewal after a price change
trigger: An existing subscriber sees a new public price but cannot determine whether or when it affects them.
action: Show the customer's actual renewal amount or basis, effective date, applicable grandfathering, and available management choices. Use the approved change policy instead of inferring their bill from the marketing page.
mechanism: Specific terms can reduce uncertainty around a consequential change.
guardrail: Do not invent grandfathering or modify a contract through copy; verify the relevant customer cohort.
measure: Retained informed renewals; price-change disputes and avoidable support.

title: Restore a scheduled cancellation deliberately
trigger: A customer whose access is still active decides to continue but cannot undo a scheduled cancellation cleanly.
action: Provide the supported resume-renewal action with the next charge and date clearly shown. Confirm the changed provider state and retain the existing account rather than creating a second subscription.
mechanism: A reversible decision can make returning to an existing commitment simpler.
guardrail: Require an explicit authorized action; do not resume billing because the customer merely signs in.
measure: Resumed useful subscriptions; accidental renewals and duplicate accounts.

title: Restore returning customers' useful context
trigger: A former subscriber returns and faces a generic new-account experience despite retained permitted data.
action: Explain what remains available under the actual retention policy, restore eligible preferences or work, and guide the user to their previous valuable workflow. Show current commercial terms before any new purchase.
mechanism: Continuity can reduce the effort needed to regain remembered value.
guardrail: Do not imply deleted data still exists or reactivate billing automatically.
measure: Reactivated accounts reaching useful use; restoration failures.

title: Recontact former customers for a real resolved reason
trigger: A former customer left for a specific missing capability or defect that has now been addressed.
action: For eligible recipients and an explicitly authorized campaign, draft a concise message explaining the actual fix and how to evaluate it. Connect the invitation to the recorded reason for leaving and offer an easy decline.
mechanism: A changed product fact can create a credible reason to reconsider.
guardrail: Verify the fix, communication permissions, suppression rules, and relevance; do not imply a personal conversation that never happened.
measure: Reactivated retained customers; opt-outs and irrelevant outreach.

title: Suppress promotions during unresolved customer problems
trigger: A customer waiting for a refund or serious support resolution keeps receiving upgrade and renewal promotions.
action: Coordinate lifecycle state so promotional prompts pause while the relevant issue is unresolved, while required service notices remain accurate. Resume appropriate communication only after the state genuinely changes.
mechanism: Consistent treatment can prevent promotional pressure from worsening a trust problem.
guardrail: Do not hide essential billing notices or infer sensitive circumstances; use verified account and support state.
measure: Resolved accounts retained; complaint escalation and opt-outs.

title: Measure useful outcomes in account health
trigger: The product labels an account healthy because of frequent logins while its core jobs repeatedly fail.
action: Base visible success check-ins and support prioritization on verified customer outcomes and stated goals. Ask an optional focused question when activity is high but useful results are absent, then address the actual blockage.
mechanism: Attention to achieved value can uncover dissatisfaction concealed by superficial engagement.
guardrail: Do not treat correlation as proof or label a customer unsuccessful without context.
measure: Retained accounts achieving goals; false alarms and unwanted interventions.

title: Let customers establish a useful recurring routine
trigger: The product solves a recurring job, but customers repeatedly forget to return at the moment it matters.
action: Let users define an appropriate recurring workflow or review cadence and make the next useful task easy to resume. Offer reminders only when requested through the authorized preference-based process.
mechanism: A customer-chosen routine can connect the subscription to an existing recurring need.
guardrail: Avoid streak penalties, artificial chores, and unsolicited reminders; keep scheduling and opt-out controls understandable.
measure: Repeated valuable use; reminder fatigue and unused automation.

title: Make accumulated work easy to retrieve
trigger: Subscribers have valuable past work in the product but repeatedly fail to find the item they need.
action: Provide permission-aware search and useful filters for the actual artifacts, with clear titles, dates, ownership, and a direct route back into the saved work. Let customers pin important items without requiring them to reorganize everything.
mechanism: Retrievable accumulated value can make continued use worthwhile and reduce the effort of returning.
guardrail: Keep search results synchronized with deletion and access changes; never reveal another workspace's private content.
measure: Successful retrieval and retained useful use; inaccessible or unauthorized results.

title: Introduce relevant improvements inside existing workflows
trigger: Current customers miss a new capability that solves a problem they previously encountered.
action: Present a concise contextual explanation when the relevant workflow appears, showing what changed and how to use it. Make broader release notes available without interrupting unrelated tasks.
mechanism: A timely improvement can refresh the product's experienced value for an existing customer.
guardrail: Only describe shipped capabilities available to that account; avoid turning every release into a forced announcement.
measure: Adoption of useful improvements; task interruption and announcement fatigue.
